open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct, or refute by a specific encoded experiment, a finite shared-trace recession library satisfying canonical-section preservation of every active \(D_v\), \(H_r\), and protected star; safety of every positive-weight candidate; simultaneous-collar compatibility; translated-uniform tails; and an input-computable refinement schedule whose total ledger vanishes and for which \(N_j/L_j\to0\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The available finite active-set geometry controls forward motion from a fixed mean, but it does not show that canonical sections preserve every active semantic region and the separated-risk set throughout protected stars. Equality of shared face vertices does not control the actual face--cone rules on simultaneous collar supports. The frozen assumptions also provide neither translated-uniform guard and normal-base tail bounds nor a recurrence for the growing number of charged refined cells.
open_obligations.attempted: The preceding construction used one smoothed ancestor, one common rational simplicial fan, common raywise Foelner factors, and shared finite-element face variables. These yield path-independent operators and explicit translation-boundary ratios. The collar induction nevertheless becomes circular if its trace is defined from the already-glued rule, while constant lower-skeleton extension can activate an unsafe candidate. By directive, no further generic averaging reroll is asserted as a proof.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Starting from the single ancestor \(q_s=K*\phi_{s^2\Sigma}\),
\(\text{lem:common\mbox{-}ray\mbox{-}folner\mbox{-}coherence}\) proves that,
for every face inclusion \(\tau\preceq\sigma\),
\[
q_{\sigma,L}
=
\left(
\prod_{\varrho\in\mathscr R(\sigma)\setminus\mathscr R(\tau)}
\mathsf A_{\varrho,L}
\right)q_{\tau,L},
\]
independently of the incidence path, together with the bounds
\[
\left\|q_{\sigma,L}(w+a\varrho)-q_{\sigma,L}(w)\right\|_1
\leq2\min\{1,a/L\}
\]
and
\[
\left|F^f_{\sigma,L}(w+a\varrho)-F^f_{\sigma,L}(w)\right|
\leq R_f\min\{1,a/L\}.
\]
The smoothing, one-chart averaging, and weighted path results separately give
\[
R_f\min\{1,s^2\sqrt{d/8}\},
\qquad
\frac{R_fk}{T\sqrt{2\pi}},
\qquad
\sum_e\Gamma_{C,e}^f+\frac{R_f}{2}\omega(h)
\]
for each fixed finite library.  These conclusions control a single smoothed
ancestor, individual chart averages, path-independent common-ray operators,
and the error of an already specified finite gluing family.  They do not prove
canonical-section preservation, safety of every positive-weight candidate,
compatibility throughout simultaneous collar supports, translated-uniform
tails, or a computable growing-refinement schedule.  Hence the simultaneous
effective-compatible-density conclusion remains open.

prose_updates.tldr: The unconditional contribution consists of three proved pieces: common-ray Foelner operators are path-independent and have explicit translation-boundary ratios; Carter's bounded-ratio kernels give fixed-base compact multinomial transfer with separately displayed semantic, covariance, and \(C_{2/\kappa}m\log(m)/\sqrt n\) charges; and compact exhaustion gives a global minimax lower limit together with two-sided convergence on diagonally selected expanding lawful windows, but no global upper limit. Replayable moving-offset transfer and CertGluePFL termination remain conditional on an affirmative resolution of the effective-compatible-density question or on a separately proved sufficient compatibility package.

project_justification.gap: Carter's bounded-ratio comparison controls a fixed positive-cell multinomial experiment and its matched Gaussian experiment, but it does not construct a replayable Gaussian rule for moving causal truth regions or control parameters escaping every compact set. At recession, common-ray commutativity does not control the Gaussian-weighted difference between incident face and cone rules on simultaneous collars. The remaining open question asks for canonical-section safety, safety of every positive-weight candidate, translated-uniform tails, and an input-computable growing-refinement schedule whose entire ledger vanishes.
project_justification.niche: Finite-label partial-identification inference combines discontinuous completed labels, intersecting unbounded recession faces, and a global honesty constraint. Equality on a geometric face does not control all candidates mixed on nearby simultaneous collars, while compact local asymptotics cannot detect a hard seam escaping to infinity. The proved compact/windowed theory and the unanswered compatibility-density question at unbounded recession seams are therefore mathematically distinct.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves common-ray operator coherence, Carter-based fixed-base compact transfer with separate semantic and covariance terms, a global minimax lower limit, and two-sided convergence on diagonally selected expanding lawful windows. It does not prove global effective compatible density. The corresponding open-ended question lists the five certificates still required. Replayable moving-offset rules and CertGluePFL termination are asserted only under an affirmative answer or a separately proved sufficient compatibility package.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: On every fixed compact set, base convergence and the centered local expansion imply eventual positive cells and lawful causal parameters. Carter then contributes only the bounded-ratio experiment error; the score mean, covariance, active-face remainder, rational offset, and semantic-union displacement are charged separately. A diagonal argument selects expanding lawful windows after the required compact moduli have passed. The present hypotheses prove that such a selection exists, but do not compute the compact moduli, lawful-ball inclusion radii, or required suprema, and no premise controls a label boundary inserted beyond the selected window.

prose_updates.related_work: Carter (2002, Theorem 1 and Sections 2--6) supplies the bounded-ratio comparison between fixed positive-cell multinomial experiments and their matched multivariate normal experiments through parameter-independent kernels. The present fixed-base compact result separately charges semantic geometry, covariance replacement, and \(C_{2/\kappa}m\log(m)/\sqrt n\); for a supplied Gaussian rule, the moving-offset comparison additionally uses the paper's affine-slack geometry, while finite replayability remains conditional. Chen and Flores (2015, Propositions 1--2 and Section 4) supply the survivor--complier Job Corps setting. Blanco, Flores, and Flores-Lagunes (2013, Assumptions A--B and Proposition 1) study randomized treatment among the always employed. Their model embeds in the present setting only after perfect compliance \(D^{\mathrm{pot}}(z)=z\), \(s(x)=+1\), restriction to a finite wage grid, and positive always-employed mass, when \(\mathrm{ASC}=\mathrm{EE}\); there is no full-class inclusion or automatic sharpness transfer outside that restriction. Day and Markov--Kakutani invariant-mean theory and Namioka's 1964 Foelner conditions concern a single amenable commuting action and supply neither an input-computable modulus nor semantic coverage, separated-risk safety, translated-tail control, or branching-refinement complexity.
prose_updates.interpretation: The Gaussian experiment is the valid local decision target on each fixed lawful direction window. Carter's bounded-ratio kernels and the paper's geometry compare a supplied Gaussian rule with the multinomial experiment on such a compact; producing a finite replayable moving-offset Gaussian rule remains conditional on effective compatible density or a separately proved sufficient compatibility package. Compact exhaustion gives a global minimax lower limit and two-sided convergence only along diagonally selected expanding lawful windows; the compact hypotheses provide existence of the diagonal selection, not an algorithm for it, and they imply no global upper limit. The common-ray library is an algebraically coherent recession representation, not a compatibility-density theorem.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Effective compatible density is unresolved under the standing assumptions. One unproved obligation is to show that every canonical chart section remains in each required \(D_v\), \(H_r\), and declared chart-neighborhood incidence region. The remaining obligations are safety of every positive-weight candidate; exact overlap traces or a valid Gaussian-weighted face-cone discrepancy bound on simultaneous supports; translated-uniform guard and normal-base tails; and computed refinement counts \(N_j\) with schedules \(L_j,B_j,\delta_j\) for which every accumulated error vanishes and \(N_j/L_j\) tends to zero. No refinement-independent ledger constant is assumed. The four-label milliscale certificate and unconditional global CertGluePFL termination therefore remain unresolved.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal target is the same-law joint identified set and is only contained in the product of coordinatewise sharp endpoint intervals; no Cartesian joint sharpness is claimed. Carter-backed sampled-data conclusions are fixed-compact or expanding-window statements. Compact exhaustion proves a global lower limit and two-sided windowed convergence, but neither a global \(\limsup\) nor a globally honest unbounded sampled-data primal. The paper proves common-ray operator identities, Gaussian smoothing, one-chart averaging, and the weighted telescoping inequality for any already specified finite family with certified edge discrepancies. It does not prove existence of finite families whose total compatibility ledger vanishes. Effective compatible density remains an open-ended question, and CertGluePFL termination and replayable global Gaussian certification remain conditional.

statement_notes.gap: Common-ray path independence and single-chart estimates do not establish canonical-section preservation, safety of every positive-weight candidate, compatibility on simultaneous collars, translated-uniform tails, or a computable refinement schedule with a vanishing total ledger.

proofs.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: parameter-independent Le Cam transfer, affine-score Gaussian comparison, and finite-arrangement perturbation.}
Put \(D_n=\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(0)\}\), \(I_n=B'D_n^{-1}B\), and \(\Sigma_n=I_n^{-1}\).  The equality \(p_n(0)=p_0\), \(\min_j(p_0)_j\geq\kappa>0\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(B)=d\) imply that every displayed inverse exists and, in fact, \(\Sigma_n=\Sigma_0\).  By \(\mathrm{prop:carter\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}m\mbox{-}positive\mbox{-}cell}\), on the fixed compact set \(C\) Carter's parameter-independent kernel has total-variation error
\[
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{Car},n}
 =C_{2/\kappa}\frac{m\log m}{\sqrt n}.
 \tag{1}
\]
If \(Y_n\) denotes the matched normal vector, apply the fixed affine score map
\[
 S_n(Y_n)=\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}
 \frac{Y_n-np_n(0)}{\sqrt n}.
 \tag{2}
\]
At parameter \(u\), (2) has law \(N_d\{\mu_n(u),V_n(u)\}\), where
\[
 \mu_n(u)=\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}sqrt n\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\},
 \tag{3}
\]
\[
 V_n(u)=\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}
 [\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(u)\}-p_n(u)p_n(u)']
 D_n^{-1}B\Sigma_n.
 \tag{4}
\]
Define the centered expansion modulus
\[
 d_n(C)=\sup_{u\in C}
 \left\|\sqrt n\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}-Bu\right\|_2.
 \tag{5}
\]
Since \(\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}B=I_d\),
\[
 \sup_{u\in C}\|\mu_n(u)-u\|_2
 \leq\|\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}d_n(C).
 \tag{6}
\]
The local-expansion assumption makes (5) tend to zero.  Base positivity, (4), and \(\mathrm{lem:compact\mbox{-}moving\mbox{-}remainder\mbox{-}covariance}\) give
\[
 \sup_{u\in C}\|V_n(u)-\Sigma_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{7}
\]

For positive definite \(V\), set
\[
 \mathsf H^2(\mu,V;u,\Sigma_0)=2-2
 \frac{|V|^{1/4}|\Sigma_0|^{1/4}}
 {|(V+\Sigma_0)/2|^{1/2}}
 \exp\!\left[-\frac18(\mu-u)'
 \{(V+\Sigma_0)/2\}^{-1}(\mu-u)\right].
 \tag{8}
\]
Completing the square in the product of the two Gaussian densities gives (8) as twice one minus their Hellinger affinity.  Cauchy--Schwarz gives total variation at most \(\mathsf H\).  Hence the explicit covariance-and-score replacement charge
\[
 \operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)=
 \sup_{u\in C}\min\{1,
 \mathsf H(\mu_n(u),V_n(u);u,\Sigma_0)\}
 \tag{9}
\]
tends to zero by (6)--(7), compactness, and eventual uniform positive definiteness.

Let
\[
 \delta_n(C)=\max_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}
 \sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|,
 \qquad x_n(C)=d_n(C)+\delta_n(C),
 \tag{10}
\]
where the maximum is zero if the active list is empty.  Because \(p_n(0)=p_0\), every moving offset is zero.  The exact slack identity and \(\mathrm{lem:finite\mbox{-}completed\mbox{-}arrangement\mbox{-}stability}\) therefore match every finite-sample coverage role on \(C\) to the same incident Gaussian-label role at Mahalanobis displacement at most \(H_Cx_n(C)\).  Its directed-Hausdorff conclusion gives the same bound, after enlarging the finite active-set constant \(H_C\), for restoration of a separated-risk role.  For \(r_0>0\), this restoration is obtained by radial dilation inside the relevant homogeneous cone: if the reference distance is \(r_0-\gamma\), multiplication by \(r_0/(r_0-\gamma)\) restores distance \(r_0\), and compactness of \(C\) bounds the displacement linearly in \(\gamma\) when \(\gamma<r_0/2\).  For \(r_0=0\), a uniquely labelled point has positive distance from the finite closed union of rival semantic cones; incident open chambers approximate equality faces, and the completed-face convention retains every required coverage label.  These finitely many alternatives are exactly what the rational active-set enumeration entering \(H_C\) checks.

Two equal-covariance Gaussian shifts whose means are at Mahalanobis distance \(a\) have total-variation distance \(2\Phi(a/2)-1\leq a/\sqrt{2\pi}\).  Absorb this numerical factor in \(H_C\).  If \(x_n(C)\leq\tau\), the only unmatched sign patterns lie in the protected Gaussian boundary band, of probability at most \(\mathfrak b_0(\tau)\).  If \(x_n(C)>\tau\), the trivial bound one applies.  Combining these facts with (1), (9), and \(\mathrm{lem:bounded\mbox{-}semantic\mbox{-}transfer\mbox{-}by\mbox{-}tv}\), first for \(\mathbf 1\{v\in A\}\) and then for \(0\leq\ell_0(A)\leq1\), yields exactly
\[
 \mathcal E_n(C,\tau)
 =\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Car},n}+\mathfrak b_0(\tau)
 +H_Cx_n(C)+\mathbf 1\{x_n(C)>\tau\}
 +\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C).
 \tag{11}
\]

We now sharpen (11) as required.  Define the finite constant
\[
 A_0=
 \sum_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}
 \frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}\{a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{1/2}},
 \tag{12}
\]
with the empty sum equal to zero.  Every denominator in (12) is positive because \(a_j\neq0\) and \(\Sigma_0\succ0\).  From the definition of \(\mathfrak b_0\) and \(\min\{1,z\}\leq z\) for \(z\geq0\),
\[
 \mathfrak b_0(x)\leq A_0x\qquad(x\geq0).
 \tag{13}
\]
Choose \(\tau=x_n(C)\).  Then the indicator in (11) is zero, and (13) gives the input-displayed bound
\[
 \mathcal E_n\{C,x_n(C)\}
 \leq C_{2/\kappa}\frac{m\log m}{\sqrt n}
 +(H_C+A_0)x_n(C)+\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C).
 \tag{14}
\]
The compact remainder lemma gives \(\delta_n(C)\to0\), while (5) and (9) tend to zero by the declared assumptions.  Thus the right side of (14) tends to zero, which also proves the iterated limit asserted in the theorem.  Equation (14) is not called \(O(n^{-1/2})\): no such conclusion follows without rates for \(x_n(C)\) and the covariance replacement.

\textbf{Technique: compatible affine-offset lifting followed by the unconditional Carter--geometry lemma and a conditional certificate invocation.}
Let \(A_\Psi\) have rows \(\alpha_j'\), \(j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}\).  Since every active cut has \(\psi_j(p_0)=0\),
\[
 c_n=A_\Psi\sqrt n\{p_n(0)-p_0\}.
 \tag{15}
\]
The local-family affine-hull condition places the vector after \(A_\Psi\) in \(L_{\mathrm{ASC}}=\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\).  The definition of \(\mathcal K_0\) therefore yields
\[
 c_n\in\mathcal K_0\qquad\text{for every }n.
 \tag{16}
\]
The effective offset encoding returns the rational \(\widehat c_n\) in the statement.  For every active facet, the exact moving-slack identity gives
\[
 \zeta_{n,j}(u)-(\widehat c_{n,j}+a_j'u)
 =(c_{n,j}-\widehat c_{n,j})+e_{n,j}(u),
 \tag{17}
\]
and consequently
\[
 \max_j\sup_{u\in C}
 |\zeta_{n,j}(u)-(\widehat c_{n,j}+a_j'u)|
 \leq\delta_n(C)+\xi_n\leq\overline\chi_n(C).
 \tag{18}
\]

We verify that the Gaussian object used conditionally is lawful.  Rational linear algebra applied to the rational image description of \(\mathcal K_0\) gives a rational \(z_n\in L_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) with \(A_\Psi z_n=\widehat c_n\).  Relative interiority implies that, for every fixed \(u\),
\[
 p_0+t(z_n+Bu)\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}
 \quad\text{for all sufficiently small }t>0.
 \tag{19}
\]
Indeed, in a relative-facet representation \(Eq=e\), \(F_iq\leq f_i\), one has \(E(z_n+Bu)=0\), while every slack \(f_i-F_ip_0\) is positive; choosing \(t\) below the minimum of the finitely many positive ratios proves (19).  Every feasible optimal branch completion at (19) has active signs
\[
 \operatorname{sgn}\{\alpha_j'(z_n+Bu)\}
 =\operatorname{sgn}(\widehat c_{n,j}+a_j'u),
 \tag{20}
\]
with equality assigned to every incident completion.  Hence the offset semantic cells cover \(\mathbb R^d\).

If the active list is nonempty, choose a strict chamber direction \(y\) of the finite homogeneous arrangement.  Along \(ty\), every fixed offset in (20) is dominated by its nonzero homogeneous slack.  For each rival component there is a nonzero rational row \(a' g\leq b\) and constants \(\gamma>0\), \(C<\infty\) such that its gap at \(ty\) is at least \(t\gamma-C\).  For every point \(g\) in that rival component, Cauchy--Schwarz in the \(\Sigma_0\) metric gives
\[
 t\gamma-C\leq a'(ty-g)
 \leq\|a\|_{\Sigma_0}\|ty-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}.
 \tag{21}
\]
The denominator is positive because \(a\neq0\) and \(\Sigma_0\succ0\).  The finite minimum of (21) exceeds \(r_0\) for sufficiently large \(t\), proving a nonempty separated domain.  If there are no active cuts, \(\mathrm{prop:tangent\mbox{-}fan\mbox{-}global\mbox{-}cover}\) gives one global semantic label and the conclusion is immediate.  Positivity of \(p_0\) and full column rank of \(B\) give \(\Sigma_0\succ0\); all cell and covariance data are rational.  Thus \(\mathfrak G_0(\widehat c_n)\in\mathfrak E\).

Now supply an arbitrary Gaussian rule on this offset experiment.  Equations (17)--(18), Carter's positive-cell bound, and the score-normal covariance enclosure meet every hypothesis of \(\mathrm{lem:moving\mbox{-}offset\mbox{-}carter\mbox{-}geometry}\).  That unconditional lemma gives the additive charge
\[
 \Delta_n(C)=C_{2/\kappa}\frac{|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|}{\sqrt n}
 +\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)
 +(H_C+2A_0)\overline\chi_n(C).
 \tag{22}
\]
No compatibility-density assertion is used in (15)--(22).

For the final replayability clause, assume explicitly the affirmative construction and bounds stated in \(\mathrm{oeq:effective\mbox{-}compatible\mbox{-}density}\), or a separately proved package supplying the same finite-library inequalities.  The conditional \(\mathrm{thm:certglue\mbox{-}termination}\) applied to \(\mathfrak G_0(\widehat c_n)\) then returns a finite Gaussian rule, its atomic dual, and outward chart, tail, quadrature, rounding, and repair entries.  Apply the parameter-independent forward Carter kernel to that rule.  The triangle inequality and (22) bound both the coverage deficit and the normalized separated-risk excess by \(\Delta_n(C)\) plus those nonnegative outward entries.

The supplied enclosure tends to zero, so the linear term in (22) vanishes; the Carter term \(C_{2/\kappa}|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|/\sqrt n\) vanishes, and the covariance term vanishes by the compact covariance lemma.  Under the stated affirmative conditional premise, request certificate, tail, integration, rounding, and repair accuracies successively below \(1/n\).  Their finite searches terminate by the premise and by the CertGlue theorem, so every remaining outward entry tends to zero.  This proves the conditional replayable conclusion.  Every infimum and supremum used in the transfer is restricted to \(C\); nothing in the argument asserts honesty or risk control on the exterior unbounded regions.

\textbf{Technique: diagonal compact exhaustion, finite-support dual transfer, and exact windowwise repair.}
Write \(B_k=\{u:\|u\|_2\leq k\}\).  Fix \(k\).  The compact causal-domain lemma gives
\[
 B_k\subseteq\mathcal U_n
 \tag{23}
\]
eventually.  The positive-cell proposition gives, eventually,
\[
 \min_{u\in B_k}\min_{j\in\mathcal J}p_{n,j}(u)\geq\kappa/2.
 \tag{24}
\]
For each fixed \(\ell\leq k\), local expansion, zero-offset centering, and the compact remainder-and-covariance lemma make every term in \(\mathscr E_n(\ell)\) tend to zero.  There are only finitely many \(\ell\leq k\); hence (23), (24), and \(\mathscr E_n(\ell)\leq1/\ell\) hold simultaneously for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The maximum defining \(R_n^\diamond\) is then at least \(k\).  Since \(k\) was arbitrary,
\[
 R_n^\diamond\longrightarrow\infty.
 \tag{25}
\]
This is a diagonal existence argument.  It does not compute the first index at which (23), (24), or the compact suprema pass their tests.  At the selected radius, however, the defining inequalities imply that the aggregate comparison error, denoted \(\rho_n\), satisfies \(\rho_n\to0\).

Let \(L<M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\).  Atomic duality supplies a finite Gaussian dual certificate \(\mu\) of value greater than \(L\).  Its finitely many coverage and risk support points lie in some \(B_k\).  Zero-offset centering and finite-arrangement stability realize each coverage atom carrying label \(v\) by a point of \(D_{n,v}\cap B_{k+1}\) at Mahalanobis distance tending to zero.  An equality atom is realized separately for every constraint role; the completed-face convention preserves all incident labels.

For a risk atom \(h\in H_{r_0}\), a lawful realization may also be chosen in \(H_{n,r_0}\).  If \(r_0>0\), the zero-offset semantic cells are cones and distance to each rival cone is positively homogeneous.  Replace \(h\) by \((1+t_n)h\), with \(t_n\downarrow0\) but large enough that the added distance margin dominates twice the directed-Hausdorff error.  Finite-arrangement stability then gives a nearby multinomial point whose distance from every rival union is at least \(r_0\).  If \(r_0=0\), uniqueness of the label at \(h\) and closedness of the finite rival union give
\[
 \operatorname{dist}_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}
 \left(h,\bigcup_{v'\neq v}D_{v'}^0\right)>0,
 \tag{26}
\]
so the same conclusion holds once the arrangement error is smaller than half (26).  By (25), all finitely many realized atoms lie inside \(B_{R_n^\diamond}\) eventually.

Apply Carter's reverse parameter-independent kernel to an arbitrary window-honest multinomial rule and then apply the score and covariance maps.  The bounded semantic-transfer lemma changes the finite dual objective by at most \(A_\mu\rho_n\), where \(A_\mu<\infty\) is the sum of the finitely many absolute dual coefficients.  Weak duality therefore gives
\[
 M_n^\diamond\geq L-A_\mu\rho_n.
 \tag{27}
\]
First let \(n\to\infty\), then let \(L\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\), to obtain
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n^\diamond
 \geq M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
 \tag{28}
\]

For the reverse inequality, fix \(a>0\).  Attainment gives a measurable \(K^a\in\mathcal C_{\eta_0}\) satisfying
\[
 \sup_{h\in H_{r_0}}E_h\ell_0\{K^a(W_0)\}
 \leq M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a.
 \tag{29}
\]
The forward Carter kernel, Gaussian total-variation comparison, and finite-arrangement matching apply to every measurable randomized rule; no finite representation of \(K^a\) is needed.  By the defining tests for the selected window, its transfer has window coverage at least \(1-\eta_0-\rho_n\) and window separated risk at most
\[
 M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a+\rho_n.
 \tag{30}
\]
At a separated-set boundary with \(r_0>0\), radial dilation restores distance \(r_0\), and the displacement is bounded by \(2R_n^\diamond\gamma/r_0\) when the distance deficit is \(\gamma<r_0/2\); this is one of the finite-arrangement terms tested before the radius is admitted.  When \(r_0=0\), (26) applies pointwise and incident chamber approximation plus Gaussian-shift continuity handles equality faces.  Thus (30) does not replace \(r_0\) by \(r_0-o(1)\).

Apply exact full-set mixing on the window with
\[
 q_n=\frac{\rho_n}{\eta_0+\rho_n}.
 \tag{31}
\]
The denominator is positive because \(\eta_0>0\), and
\[
 (1-q_n)(1-\eta_0-\rho_n)+q_n=1-\eta_0.
 \tag{32}
\]
Since \(0\leq\ell_0\leq1\), (30)--(32) yield
\[
 M_n^\diamond\leq M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a+\rho_n
 +\frac{\rho_n}{\eta_0+\rho_n}.
 \tag{33}
\]
Letting \(n\to\infty\), then \(a\downarrow0\), and combining (28) and (33), proves
\[
 M_n^\diamond\longrightarrow M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
 \tag{34}
\]

Every globally honest rule is window-honest, and its global risk supremum dominates its window risk supremum.  Therefore the two minimax definitions give
\[
 M_n\geq M_n^\diamond.
 \tag{35}
\]
Equations (34)--(35) prove the asserted global lower limit.

Conditionally on the affirmative ECD conclusion, or on a separately proved sufficient package, CertGlue supplies a replayable finite Gaussian rule and exact repair for any already specified window; its transfer follows the same equations above.  This does not make the diagonal choice of \(R_n^\diamond\) computable, because the standing hypotheses provide no algorithms for the compact suprema or lawful-ball inclusion.  Finally, \(\mathrm{lem:escaping\mbox{-}boundary\mbox{-}kill}\) exhibits arrays identical on every fixed compact but with different global upper behavior.  It therefore rules out any global \(\limsup\) conclusion from the premises used here.

\textbf{Technique: conditional effective dovetailing of sound primal and dual semidecisions.}
Assume the conditional premise in the statement; it is not derived here.  Precisely, the premise supplies a computable sequence \(\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)\downarrow0\) and finite records \(Q_j(K)\in\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,j}\) such that, for every \(K\in\mathcal C_\eta\),
\[
 c\{Q_j(K)\}\geq1-\eta-\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j),
 \tag{36}
\]
\[
 r\{Q_j(K)\}\leq R_r(K)+D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{led}}\{Q_j(K)\}\leq\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j).
 \tag{37}
\]
Here \(c(Q)\) is the infimum of all semantic coverage probabilities and \(r(Q)\) is the separated diameter risk.  The finite record also certifies the canonical-section, positive-weight safety, simultaneous-collar, translated-tail, and refinement-count facts needed for (36)--(37).  No refinement-independent ledger constant is used.

At stage \(s\), enumerate all library indices \(j\leq s\), all records in \(\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,j}\) of code length at most \(s\), all rational incidence forests and semantic projections in those records, and the first \(s\) rational choices of integration and rounding precision.  The weighted ledger gives outward rational enclosures
\[
 c^-_{Q,s}\leq c(Q),
 \qquad r(Q)\leq r^+_{Q,s}.
 \tag{38}
\]
Accept a record only after every rational polyhedral incidence, protected-neighborhood, Gaussian-tail, covariance, quadrature, and rounding check supporting (38) has passed.  Thus acceptance uses no uncertified floating-point sign.

Intersect \(c^-_{Q,s}\) with \([0,1]\), and define
\[
 \rho_{Q,s}=\max\{0,1-\eta-c^-_{Q,s}\},
 \qquad q_{Q,s}=\frac{\rho_{Q,s}}{\eta+\rho_{Q,s}}.
 \tag{39}
\]
Because \(0<\eta<1/2\),
\[
 0\leq\rho_{Q,s}\leq1-\eta<1,
 \qquad \eta+\rho_{Q,s}>0,
 \tag{40}
\]
so the division is valid.  Equations (38)--(39) imply \(c(Q)\geq1-\eta-\rho_{Q,s}\).  The exact-repair lemma makes \(Q^+=\operatorname{Repair}_{\eta,\rho_{Q,s}}(Q)\) globally honest and gives
\[
 M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
 \leq R_r(Q^+)
 \leq r^+_{Q,s}+Dq_{Q,s}.
 \tag{41}
\]
Outward rational interval arithmetic produces a rational \(U_{Q,s}\) no smaller than the last expression.

In parallel, enumerate the finite atomic duals in \(\mathrm{thm:attainment\mbox{-}atomic\mbox{-}duality}\).  Their rational weights and rationally encoded real-algebraic support points admit exact membership checks in each finite union \(D_v\) and in \(H_r\): membership and polyhedral Mahalanobis distance reduce to finitely many polynomial sign and active-set checks.  Refine the Gaussian integrations for a feasible dual \(\nu\) until a rational lower enclosure \(l^-_{\nu,s}\) is available.  Every such number is a valid lower certificate.  Put
\[
 L_s=\max_{\nu\text{ processed by }s}l^-_{\nu,s},
 \qquad
 U_s=\min_{Q\text{ accepted by }s}U_{Q,s}.
 \tag{42}
\]
Whenever both endpoints exist, weak duality and (41) give
\[
 L_s\leq M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\leq U_s.
 \tag{43}
\]

Every fixed stage terminates.  Its enumerated collections are finite, rational polyhedral feasibility and incidence are finite rational linear programs, and Gaussian integration is enclosed on a rational box by interval subdivision.  On the box, each accepted record carries a certified modulus; off the box, the recorded Gaussian tail tends effectively to zero.  Hence every requested positive enclosure width is reached after finitely many subdivisions.

Let \(K^*\) be the attaining honest rule supplied by atomic duality, so
\[
 R_r(K^*)=M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r).
 \tag{44}
\]
For rational \(\zeta>0\), sufficiently fine outward evaluation of the record supplied by (36)--(37) gives
\[
 c^-_{Q_j(K^*),s}\geq c\{Q_j(K^*)\}-\zeta,
 \qquad
 r^+_{Q_j(K^*),s}\leq r\{Q_j(K^*)\}+\zeta.
 \tag{45}
\]
Thus \(\rho_{Q_j(K^*),s}\leq\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta\), and (37), (41), and one more outward width \(\zeta\) imply
\[
 U_s\leq M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
 +D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+2\zeta
 +\frac{D\{\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta\}}
 {\eta+\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta}.
 \tag{46}
\]
The right side approaches the minimax value by first increasing \(j\) and then decreasing \(\zeta\).  Atomic duality also supplies enumerated finite lower certificates converging upward to that value.  Therefore
\[
 L_s\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r),
 \qquad \limsup_{s\to\infty}U_s\leq M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r).
 \tag{47}
\]
Together with (43), this proves that some finite stage satisfies \(U_s-L_s\leq\varepsilon\).

For the explicit cost receipt, let \(a_i(\mathfrak G,s)\) count operations of type \(i\in\{\mathrm{glue},\mathrm{cut},\mathrm{Gauss},\mathrm{LP}\}\) at stage \(s\), and let \(b(\mathfrak G,s)\) be the largest integer bit length occurring there.  Define by primitive recursion
\[
 C_i(0)=a_i(\mathfrak G,0),\qquad
 C_i(s+1)=C_i(s)+a_i(\mathfrak G,s+1),
 \tag{48}
\]
\[
 B(0)=b(\mathfrak G,0),\qquad
 B(s+1)=\max\{B(s),b(\mathfrak G,s+1)\}.
 \tag{49}
\]
Let
\[
 s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)=
 \min\{s:L_s,U_s\text{ are defined and }U_s-L_s\leq\varepsilon\}.
 \tag{50}
\]
The test is rational and (47) proves its search halts.  Hence \(s_*\) is total recursive under the conditional premise.  Set
\[
 N_i(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)=C_i\{s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Bit}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)=B\{s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\}.
 \tag{51}
\]
Archive at stage \(s_*\) the repaired primal attaining the finite minimum and the finite atomic dual attaining the finite maximum in (42).  Equations (43), (50), and (51) give the endpoints, gap, termination, replayability, and five-part receipt.  The only use of compatibility density was the expressly conditional input (36)--(37); the proof does not answer the OEQ.

\textbf{Technique: composition of exact finite-fiber identification, rational tangent geometry, and the compact transfer results.}
Let \(P_0\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) and \(p_0=p(P_0)\).  The assignment, support, randomization, three consistency conditions, no-defiers, complier-conditional selection monotonicity, and aggregate positivity are the separately declared restrictions defining \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\).  In particular,
\[
 M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\geq m_*>0,
 \tag{52}
\]
so every conditional quantile in the target has a positive denominator.

The causal polyhedralization theorem identifies the selected-complier submeasures and proves that the response-type polytope represents exactly \(\mathcal F(p_0)\).  The lower- and upper-endpoint attainment propositions give, for each fixed \(t\in\mathcal T\), same-law witnesses satisfying
\[
 Q_{1,P_t^-(p_0)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^-(p_0)}(t)
 =\underline\Delta(t;p_0),
 \tag{53}
\]
\[
 Q_{1,P_t^+(p_0)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^+(p_0)}(t)
 =\overline\Delta(t;p_0).
 \tag{54}
\]
For an arbitrary single \(P\in\mathcal F(p_0)\), the definitions of the infimum and supremum give
\[
 \underline\Delta(t;p_0)
 \leq Q_{1,P}(t)-Q_{0,P}(t)
 \leq\overline\Delta(t;p_0).
 \tag{55}
\]
Taking all coordinates and then all compatible laws in (55) proves
\[
 \Theta_{\mathrm{ASC}}(p_0)
 \subseteq\prod_{t\in\mathcal T}
 [\underline\Delta(t;p_0),\overline\Delta(t;p_0)].
 \tag{56}
\]
The witnesses in (53)--(54) may depend on \(t\) and on the endpoint, so (56) is only an outer rectangle and not a Cartesian sharpness assertion.

Under relative interiority and tangent-image compatibility, the tangent-cover proposition gives \(\bigcup_vD_v^0=\mathbb R^d\).  For every nonzero \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), multinomial positivity and full column rank of \(B\) give
\[
 x'I_0x=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}
 \frac{\{(Bx)_j\}^2}{(p_0)_j}>0.
 \tag{57}
\]
Thus \(I_0\succ0\), \(\Sigma_0=I_0^{-1}\succ0\), and rationality of \(p_0\) and \(B\) makes \(\Sigma_0\) rational.  The radius proposition supplies \(H_{r_0}\neq\varnothing\).  These facts are exactly the cover, covariance, and separated-domain conditions of \(\mathfrak E\), so
\[
 \mathfrak G_0\in\mathfrak E.
 \tag{58}
\]

The fixed-stratum theorem gives Carter's compact comparison and the sharpened charge \(C_{2/\kappa}m\log(m)/\sqrt n+(H_C+A_0)x_n(C)+\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\), with semantic and covariance terms displayed separately.  For moving offsets, the unconditional moving-offset Carter--geometry lemma applies to any supplied Gaussian rule and yields the linear charge \((H_C+2A_0)\overline\chi_n(C)\).  The existence of a finite replayable Gaussian rule at the moving offset is not inferred from this comparison: it follows only under the affirmative ECD conclusion, or under a separately proved sufficient compatibility package, through the conditional CertGlue theorem and the moving-offset theorem.

Under zero-offset centering, compact exhaustion proves
\[
 M_n^\diamond\longrightarrow M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0),
 \qquad
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n
 \geq M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
 \tag{59}
\]
The radii in (59) are selected by a diagonal existence argument; no modulus for the required compact suprema or lawful-ball inclusion is supplied by the standing assumptions.  Under the same ECD conditional, CertGlue returns the replayable Gaussian primal, atomic dual, outward endpoints, and repair ingredients at any already selected window.  Finally, the escaping-boundary lemma proves that compact comparison cannot supply a global sampled-data upper bound.  Therefore (59) is not enlarged to a global \(\limsup\), a globally honest unbounded transferred primal, or a two-sided global minimax limit.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix a rational compact polytope \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\).  Suppose the multinomial interior, base-convergence, and compact local-expansion conditions hold, \(c_n,\widehat c_n\) lie eventually in one compact subset of \(\mathcal K_0\), and \(\|\widehat c_n-c_n\|_\infty\leq\xi_n\).  Define
\[
 d_n(C)=\sup_{u\in C}\left\|\sqrt n\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}-Bu\right\|_2,
 \qquad
 \delta_n(C)=\max_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|,
\]
with the maximum equal to zero for an empty active list, and put \(\chi_n(C)=d_n(C)+\delta_n(C)+\xi_n\).  Let a supplied rational number \(\overline\chi_n(C)\) satisfy \(\overline\chi_n(C)\geq\chi_n(C)\).  For any supplied Gaussian rule \(G_n\) on the completed offset regions \(D_v^0(\widehat c_n)\), suppose its Gaussian semantic coverage is at least \(1-\eta_0-\alpha_n\) and its normalized separated risk is at most \(R_n^G+\beta_n\).  Then a parameter-independent Carter transfer produces a multinomial rule \(K_n\) on \(C\) with semantic coverage at least
\[
 1-\eta_0-\alpha_n-\Delta_n(C)
\]
and normalized separated risk at most
\[
 R_n^G+\beta_n+\Delta_n(C),
\]
where
\[
 \Delta_n(C)=C_{2/\kappa}\frac{|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|}{\sqrt n}
 +\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)
 +(H_C+2A_0)\overline\chi_n(C),
 \qquad
 A_0=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}
 \frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}\{a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{1/2}}.
\]
Here coverage and risk are restricted respectively to \(D_{n,v}\cap C\) and \(H_{n,r_0}\cap C\).  The conclusion is unconditional on effective compatible density and does not assert that the supplied Gaussian rule has a finite certificate.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: exact affine-slack coupling and a linear Gaussian anti-concentration charge.}
For every active facet,
\[
 \zeta_{n,j}(u)-(\widehat c_{n,j}+a_j'u)
 =(c_{n,j}-\widehat c_{n,j})+e_{n,j}(u).
 \tag{60}
\]
Consequently the uniform slack perturbation on \(C\) is at most \(\delta_n(C)+\xi_n\leq\overline\chi_n(C)\).  The finite completed-arrangement lemma, on the common compact offset set, matches each actual coverage role and each separated-risk role to its \(\widehat c_n\)-offset counterpart with Mahalanobis displacement at most \(H_C\overline\chi_n(C)\), after the finite directed-Hausdorff and separated-set restoration constants are included in \(H_C\).  Equality faces lose no label because they belong to every incident completion.

For \(W_0\sim N_d(h,\Sigma_0)\), the scalar \(\widehat c_{n,j}+a_j'W_0\) has variance \(a_j'\Sigma_0a_j>0\).  Its density is bounded uniformly in its mean by \(\{2\pi a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{-1/2}\).  Therefore, for \(s\geq0\),
\[
 \Pr_h\{|\widehat c_{n,j}+a_j'W_0|\leq s\}
 \leq\min\left\{1,
 \frac{2s}{\sqrt{2\pi}\{a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{1/2}}\right\}.
 \tag{61}
\]
The union bound and \(\min\{1,z\}\leq z\) give
\[
 \mathfrak b_0(s)\leq A_0s.
 \tag{62}
\]
Use the supplied enclosure as the comparison threshold, \(\tau_n=\overline\chi_n(C)\).  Since \(\chi_n(C)\leq\tau_n\), the indicator \(\mathbf1\{\chi_n(C)>\tau_n\}\) is zero.  Every sign mismatch is contained in a band of width at most \(\tau_n+\chi_n(C)\leq2\overline\chi_n(C)\), so (62) charges it by
\[
 \mathfrak b_0\{\tau_n+\chi_n(C)\}
 \leq2A_0\overline\chi_n(C).
 \tag{63}
\]

On \(C\), the positive-cell proposition supplies Carter's parameter-independent kernel with error \(C_{2/\kappa}|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|/\sqrt n\).  To expose the covariance replacement, put \(D_n=\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(0)\}\), \(\Sigma_n=\{B'D_n^{-1}B\}^{-1}\), and apply to the matched normal vector \(Y_n\) the score map
\[
 S_n(Y_n)=\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}
 \frac{Y_n-np_n(0)}{\sqrt n}.
\]
Its mean is \(\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}\sqrt n\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}\), and its covariance is
\[
 \Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}
 [\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(u)\}-p_n(u)p_n(u)']
 D_n^{-1}B\Sigma_n.
\]
The compact local expansion and the compact covariance lemma bound the total variation from \(N_d(u,\Sigma_0)\) by the explicitly defined Hellinger term \(\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\).  Gaussian translation for the matched means and the arrangement displacement contributes \(H_C\overline\chi_n(C)\).  Apply the bounded semantic-transfer lemma to the indicator \(\mathbf1\{v\in A\}\) and to \(\ell_0(A)\in[0,1]\).  Adding the Carter, covariance, displacement, and band charges in their outward directions gives
\[
 \Delta_n(C)=C_{2/\kappa}\frac{|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|}{\sqrt n}
 +\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)
 +(H_C+2A_0)\overline\chi_n(C).
 \tag{64}
\]
Adding (64) to the supplied Gaussian coverage deficit \(\alpha_n\) and risk excess \(\beta_n\) proves the two asserted inequalities.  This proof begins with an arbitrary supplied Gaussian rule and nowhere invokes compatible density or CertGlue.

added_lemmas.statement: In the binary randomized-treatment sample-selection model of Blanco, Flores, and Flores-Lagunes, Assumptions A--B impose randomized treatment and monotone employment selection, the always-employed principal stratum is \(EE=\{S(0)=S(1)=1\}\), and Proposition 1 gives a partial-identification result for the always-employed wage target under those restrictions.

added_lemmas.statement:
The discrete Blanco--Flores--Flores-Lagunes model has the following restricted embedding.  Take a singleton or finitely stratified covariate support, impose perfect compliance \(D^{\mathrm{pot}}(z)=z\) almost surely, set \(s(x)=+1\) for every stratum, restrict both potential wages to the finite grid \(\mathcal Y\), use known positive randomized assignment probabilities, and suppose \(P(EE)>0\), where \(EE=\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}\).  For any \(m_*\in(0,P(EE)]\), the resulting law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), and
\[
 \{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)>D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0),\ S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}=EE,
 \qquad M_{\mathrm{ASC}}=P(EE).
\]
Thus the always-selected-complier target equals the always-employed target on this restricted submodel.  There is no asserted inclusion of the unrestricted Blanco--Flores--Flores-Lagunes class in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), and Proposition 1's sharpness does not automatically transfer outside the perfect-compliance, positive-mass, finite-grid restriction.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: an explicit response-type embedding.}
Use the randomized treatment in the cited Blanco--Flores--Flores-Lagunes model as \(Z\), and define
\[
 D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=0,
 \qquad D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1.
 \tag{65}
\]
Then treatment consistency gives \(D=Z\), the no-defiers inequality holds with strict inequality for every unit, and the complier event
\[
 \mathsf C=\{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)>D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)\}
 \tag{66}
\]
has probability one.  Randomization in Assumption A of the cited model supplies conditional independence after taking \(X\) to be a singleton, or after retaining finitely many randomization strata with their known assignment probabilities.  Positivity is imposed explicitly in the proposition.

Assumption B in the cited model is monotone employment selection.  With \(s(x)=+1\), it is exactly
\[
 s(x)\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)-S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)\}
 =S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)-S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)\geq0,
 \tag{67}
\]
which is the current complier-conditional weak-selection restriction because (66) holds surely.  Define the observed selection and wage by the declared consistency maps \(S=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(D)\) and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(D)\) on \(\{S=1\}\).  The finite-grid restriction makes every latent response a member of one of the finite sets \(\mathcal R_x\).  Assigning \(\lambda_{xr}=P(X=x,R=r)\) then gives \(\lambda\geq0\), unit total mass, and \(T_0\lambda=p\).  Thus the induced observed law is represented by the current response-type fiber.

By (66),
\[
 \mathsf C\cap\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}
 =EE.
 \tag{68}
\]
Randomization, perfect compliance, and consistency also evaluate the observed-cell contrasts exactly.  Summing over the wage grid gives
\[
 q_{0x}=P\{X=x,S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=1\},
 \qquad
 q_{1x}=P\{X=x,S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}.
 \tag{69}
\]
To see the first equality, the \(Z=1,D=0\) term in the definition of \(c_{0xk}\) is zero under (65), while division of the \(Z=0,D=0\) term by its positive assignment probability removes randomization; the second equality is analogous, with the \(Z=0,D=1\) term equal to zero.  Monotonicity (67) makes \(q_{0x}\leq q_{1x}\), and hence
\[
 m_x=\min\{q_{0x},q_{1x}\}
 =P\{X=x,S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}.
 \tag{70}
\]
Summing (70) over the finite support of \(X\) gives \(M_{\mathrm{ASC}}=P(EE)\).  The assumed positivity and \(0<m_*\leq P(EE)\) verify the aggregate target-mass restriction.  Equations (65)--(70), together with randomization, positivity, and consistency, verify every defining restriction of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), proving the embedding and equality of targets.

Without (65), the current ASC event is \(EE\cap\mathsf C\), not the full always-employed event; without the finite grid, the law is outside the declared finite response-type support; and without positive \(EE\) mass, the conditional quantiles are undefined.  Moreover, the current class permits imperfect compliance and stratum-dependent selection directions.  Hence no full-class inclusion follows, and a sharpness result for the cited restricted fiber cannot identify the larger or different fiber without a new attainability argument.

Suppose \(c_n\to c\in\mathcal K_0\).  For a rational compact polytope \(C\), define
\[
 d_n(C)=\sup_{u\in C}\left\|\sqrt n\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}-Bu\right\|_2,
 \quad
 \delta_n(C)=\max_j\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|,
\]
choose \(\widehat c_n\in\mathcal K_0\cap\mathbb Q^{|\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}|}\) with \(\|\widehat c_n-c_n\|_\infty\leq\xi_n\), and put \(\chi_n(C)=d_n(C)+\delta_n(C)+\xi_n\).  Given a supplied effective rational upper enclosure \(\overline\chi_n(C)\geq\chi_n(C)\) with \(\overline\chi_n(C)\to0\), the unconditional lemma \(\mathrm{lem:moving\mbox{-}offset\mbox{-}carter\mbox{-}geometry}\) transfers any supplied Gaussian rule for \(\mathfrak G_0(\widehat c_n)\) to \(C\), with additive coverage-deficit and normalized separated-risk charge
\[
 \Delta_n(C)=C_{2/\kappa}\frac{|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|}{\sqrt n}
 +\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)
 +(H_C+2A_0)\overline\chi_n(C),
\]
where
\[
 A_0=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}
 \frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}\{a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{1/2}}.
\]
If the affirmative conclusion specified in \(\mathrm{oeq:effective\mbox{-}compatible\mbox{-}density}\), or a separately proved sufficient compatibility package yielding its displayed finite-library bounds, is available, then \(\operatorname{CertGluePFL}\) supplies such Gaussian rules and the transferred compact rule is replayable.  Its total certified excess is at most \(\Delta_n(C)\) plus the outward chart, tail, integration, rounding, and exact-repair entries, and these terms can be scheduled to vanish.  This conditional construction uses \(\widehat c_n\), not the unknown limit \(c\), and makes no honesty or risk claim outside \(C\).
proposed.justification: The theorem gives a determinate compact moving-offset comparison and makes finite rule construction conditional on the unresolved compatibility package.
proposed.gap: It neither constructs effective compatible density nor extends compact control to all unbounded finite-sample truth regions.
proposed.consumer: Drifting capacity and endpoint-program faces receive an explicit linear boundary and offset charge, with replayability only under the displayed conditional premise.
